chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Washshāʾ, from one whom he mentioned.

From Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he disliked the leftover drink of the child of zina, the Jew, the Christian, the polytheist, and everyone who opposed Islam; and the most severe of that, in his view, was the leftover drink of the nāṣib.

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: one who bears enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the hadith
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِ: one who associates partners with Allah
key_terms.سُؤْرَ: leftover drink or remaining liquid after someone has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in al-Istibṣār say about using the leftover drink of non-Muslims and the nāṣib?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding the disliked status of the leftover drink of certain categories of people. It places the leftover drink of the nāṣib as the most severely regarded among them, reflecting a gradation in legal aversion within the narration.
